counterfactual_missing_items: no pigmentation or melanocytic morphology is described
the axillary node disease is only presumed metastatic and not biopsy-confirmed
decisive_items: a 1.8 × 1.3 cm well-circumscribed, firm, non-tender, indurated lesion
the lesion reappeared at the distal aspect of the thumb stump
an enlarged ipsilateral axillary lymph node presumed to represent metastatic disease
response.rationale: C1 retains the SCC-specific firm indurated-digit lesion of R2 while adding the explicit recurrent nature on the thumb stump, making the diagnosis temporally more precise. R2 is a strong but less complete formulation. R3 relies on generic metastatic-skin-tumor evidence without melanoma-specific findings; R1 has only a nonspecific recurrent lesion; R4 uses the same generic lesion and nodal evidence with a misspelled label and no Merkel-specific support.

rejected.why: Only a nonspecific recurrent skin lesion is cited; no Merkel-specific morphologic or clinical feature is present.
Skin tumor with lymph-node metastasis is compatible, but the vignette does not describe pigmentation or other melanoma-specific features.
The label appears misspelled and the cited raw spans are generic, with no evidence specifically supporting Merkel or Merkin cell carcinoma.
